Forensic psychologists also look at specific details about the criminal's personal life. If the crimes have been committed in a certain place, the psychologist might think that the criminal has a particular hobby or interest in that place.

By putting all these details together, forensic psychologists can create a detailed profile of the criminal. This profile can help the police understand who the criminal might be and where they might be hiding.

The degree to which these profiles are accurate tends to increase with the number of data - points ( e.g. crime scenes ) that the profiler has to work with ( i.e. that are believed to be linked to the same offender ) . Profiling specific details ( e.g. a particular car model ) can not be done with any sort of accuracy unless the profiler has additional information ( e.g. physical evidence or eye - witness accounts ) which leads him / her to make such a conclusion . It is possible , however , that certain evidence may lead the profiler to suspect the criminal drives a certain type of vehicle . For example , evidence may suggest that the crime was politically motivated and the offender is an environmental protection activist .
